description: Lending guidelines and financial regulations for credit risk decision support

strong_positive_indicators: No late payments in the past 2 years

strong_negative_indicators: Three or more 90+ day delinquencies in past 2 years

medium_risk: Request additional income documentation (pay stubs, tax returns)
Require a co-signer or guarantor with strong credit
Offer a secured loan option with collateral
Apply a risk-adjusted interest rate to compensate for elevated risk
Require proof of stable employment for at least 12 months
high_risk: Refer borrower to a certified credit counseling service
Suggest debt consolidation program before reapplying in 6-12 months
Recommend a secured credit-builder product to improve credit score
Advise borrower to reduce existing debt load before reapplying
Consider offering a small secured product as a stepping stone

excellent.assessment: Excellent financial position, low debt burden

good.assessment: Good - manageable debt load relative to income

concerning.assessment: Concerning - high debt burden, increased default risk

critical.assessment: Critical - borrower likely struggling with existing obligations

high.assessment: High utilization, may indicate financial stress

critical.assessment: Critical - maxed out credit, major risk factor

regulatory_references.name: Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) - Regulation B
regulatory_references.description: Prohibits credit discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age, or receipt of public assistance. All credit decisions must be based solely on creditworthiness factors.

regulatory_references.name: Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA)
regulatory_references.description: Governs the collection, dissemination, and use of consumer credit information. Requires lenders to inform applicants when adverse action is taken based on credit reports.

regulatory_references.name: Truth in Lending Act (TILA) - Regulation Z
regulatory_references.description: Mandates clear disclosure of loan terms, costs, and annual percentage rate (APR) to protect consumers from predatory lending.

regulatory_references.name: Fair Housing Act (FHA)
regulatory_references.description: Prohibits discrimination in residential real estate lending transactions. Applies to mortgage loans and home equity products.

regulatory_references.name: Community Reinvestment Act (CRA)
regulatory_references.description: Encourages financial institutions to meet the credit needs of all communities, including low- and moderate-income neighborhoods.

regulatory_references.name: Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform Act
regulatory_references.description: Established the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) and introduced rules to prevent unfair, deceptive, or abusive lending practices.

general_lending_principles: Lenders must assess a borrower's ability-to-repay based on verified income, assets, and debt obligations
Credit decisions must be documented with clear, objective, and non-discriminatory rationale
Adverse action notices must be provided within 30 days of a credit denial
All data used in credit decisions must comply with applicable privacy and data protection laws
Risk-based pricing must be applied consistently and transparently across all applicants
